FIR in Crime No.81/2024 was registered by the Nandini Layout Police Station, Bengaluru City against the petitioner herein initially for the offence punishable under Section 363 of IPC on the basis of first information received from respondent No.2 who is the father of the victim girl.

sentences.text: During the course of investigation, the petitioner was arrested on 20.03.2024 and remanded to judicial custody.
Investigation in the case is complete and charge sheet has been filed.
5. The bail application filed by the petitioner before the Sessions Court in Crl.Misc.No.4898/2024 was dismissed on 24.06.2024.
Therefore, he is before this Court.
6. Learned counsel for the petitioner having reiterated the grounds urged in the petition has prayed to allow the petition.
Per contra, learned HCGP has opposed the petition.
8. FIR in Crime No.81/2024 was registered by the father of the victim girl aged about 17 years who was studying in II PUC after she was found missing from her house.

In the first information it is stated that the victim girl was acquainted with the petitioner and she was moving around with him and therefore the father and elders of the family of victim girl had advised her.
It is in this background, on suspicion, the petitioner was arrayed as accused in the FIR.
During the course of investigation, the victim girl was traced and her statement was recorded before the jurisdictional Magistrate under Section 164 of Cr.P.C,
The victim girl has not made any allegation against the petitioner in the said statement.
She has stated that she had left her grandmother's house and had gone to Huligemma temple and had stayed in the said temple for seven days.
Thereafter, she returned home.
In the meanwhile, there was police complaint registered.
The NC: 2024:KHC:32446 victim girl has stated that she does not know the accused and she is being forced to register a case against the petitioner.

Considering the nature of statement made by the victim girl before the jurisdictional Magistrate under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., I am of the opinion that the petitioner who is in custody from 20.03.2024 has made out a prima-facie case for grant of regular bail.

9. Accordingly, the following:
ORDER The Criminal Petition is allowed.

The petitioner is directed to be enlarged on bail in Spl.C.No.870/2024 pending on the file of Addl. City Civil & Sessions Judge & Fast Track Special Court(FTSC-II),
Bengaluru arising out of Crime No.81/2024 registered by Nandini Layout Police Station, Bengaluru City for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 376(2)(n) of IPC, Sections 5(L) & 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012,
subject to the following conditions:

3 a) Petitioner shall execute a personal bond for a sum of Rs.1,00,000 (Rupees One Lakh only) with two sureties for the likesum, to the satisfaction of the jurisdictional Court;
b) The petitioner shall appear regularly on all the dates of hearing before the Trial Court unless the Trial Court exempts his appearance for valid reasons;
c) The petitioner shall not directly or indirectly threaten or tamper with the prosecution witnesses;
d) The petitioner shall not leave the jurisdiction of the Trial Court without permission of the said Court until the case registered against him is disposed off.
Sd/-
